angularDiameterSource: Stellar radius 0.523 (+0.023/−0.021) solar radii from Torres et al. 2015, ApJ 800, 99 (2015). It is a radius from stellar characterisation, not an interferometric diameter; the angular diameter in the record is that radius at the Gaia distance.
distanceSource: Gaia EDR3 parallax 5.6336 +/- 0.0169 mas via SIMBAD (2020yCat.1350....0G): 177.51 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius: 0.523 (+0.023/−0.021) solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius, from Torres et al. 2015 (ApJ 800, 99 (2015); arXiv:1501.01101). GM from their stellar mass 0.544 solar masses times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. presentationUp: no spin axis is measured, so the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 3755 ± 90 K from Torres et al. 2015 (ApJ 800, 99; https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.01101), Table 5, KOI-0571, the radius source: a spectroscopic value it adopts from Mann et al. 2013 and Muirhead et al. 2014.
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the astronomy record's GM and radius (physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-186 (pscomppars): spectral type M1, from Quintana et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014Sci...344..277Q/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-186 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.26 dex, from Torres et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800...99T/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-186 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.26, from Torres et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800...99T/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-186 (pscomppars): age 4 Gyr, from Torres et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800...99T/abstract)
